repository.taxonomy_note: CB identifiers are defined by this audit, not upstream project identifiers.

assurance_distinctions: Policy authorization is not capability containment.
Post-action journal/manifest/gate detection is not prevention.
A local hash chain is not an external trust anchor.
A narrow child filesystem rule is not general OS isolation.

baseline.ignored_runtime_state_note: Git porcelain was clean. Ignored .ourob runtime files were not separately content-hashed before baseline verification and are outside tracked tree/lock identity.

prior_evaluation.conclusion_handling: Prior R-01..R-06 outcomes are preserved at their stated scope; this audit adds adversarial findings without rewriting prior documents.

methodology.probe_location: Detached disposable clones under /tmp/ourob-cb-audit-*; no destructive probe on live protected artifacts.
methodology.probe_transcript_note: Manual probe outcomes are recorded in this evidence; temporary clone console transcripts are not committed as separate files.

challenge_schema.per_record_rule: Every challenge record has exactly one primary status from primary_status_vocabulary. NOT_OBSERVABLE is used for unestablished fields/results, not as a pass.

enforcement_topology.request: Planner emits Invocation to Kernel.run; registry discovers Python modules and dispatches names.
enforcement_topology.declaration: SkillSpec contains name, description, parameter hints, examples, and Boolean mutating; no mandatory per-resource capability handles.
enforcement_topology.grant: Kernel policy verdict is route-level authorization. SkillContext exposes repository Path, StateStore and services; in-process skill keeps ambient UID authority.
enforcement_topology.policy_check: Kernel._authorise checks declared invocation/context; direct registry dispatch, import side effects, raw Python/stdlib calls and raw subprocess are outside this per-operation check.
enforcement_topology.execution_interface: Built-ins may use ctx.path/fsx; arbitrary plugin Python can use pathlib/os/shutil/tempfile/subprocess. run_command/run_python use run_child.
enforcement_topology.child_enforcement: Linux Landlock ABI 2 selected content/namespace writes under protected paths/.ourob/.git and permits unprotected repository dirs plus per-call temp; seccomp denies selected ownership/xattr syscalls. Descendants inherit.
enforcement_topology.child_gaps: Reads, network, general process inspection, chmod/time changes, and pre-existing hardlink aliases are not generally controlled; same UID remains.
enforcement_topology.journal: Kernel logs decisions/results, but not each raw OS operation. State APIs have guarded writes/hash chains; same process can edit files and local head directly.
enforcement_topology.verification: Manifest/journal/contracts/gates detect only specified conditions and may run after an effect; they are not a syscall broker or prevention layer.
enforcement_topology.actual_model: Model D ambient authority for in-process plugins; narrow Model-A-like normal API authorization; partial Model-B-like child write boundary; no general Model C OS sandbox.

final_conclusion.assessment: FAILED for general capability containment; PARTIALLY CONTROLLED for specific mediated routes.
basis: In-process plugins have ambient Python/OS authority and can bypass Kernel policy.
A real pre-existing hardlink alias bypassed child Landlock and changed a protected inode.
Local journal/head could be re-chained; replay accepted modified content.
Forged authorization artifacts were accepted, including a backdated event.
Normal API, canonical child write, selected child metadata, and scratch controls do work in their stated routes.

architectural_recommendations.action: Treat plugin Python as hostile: isolate each skill under a separate unprivileged worker/broker and do not pass raw repo Path, StateStore, mutable registry, or ambient credentials.
Separate writable and protected inodes with a separate filesystem/mount or isolated worktree; test and prevent pre-existing hardlink aliases, not just link creation after Landlock.
Close child metadata gaps with strong privilege separation/read-only mounts or a reviewed syscall policy that also denies protected chmod/time changes.
Move journals/anchors outside the writer trust domain; use broker-owned append-only storage and an external signature/MAC key or independently protected monotonic anchor.
Authenticate operator identity out of process; bind a grant to a nonce, expiry, exact operation/content digest, paths, repository identity, and one run.
Replace Boolean mutating metadata with a validated capability manifest; enforce schema/path declaration before dispatch and at an operation broker.
Make discovery immutable and side-effect-safe; do not import untrusted modules in privileged registry; publish immutable snapshots and avoid mutable internals as a security boundary.
Remove API keys from arbitrary skill child environments; use a scoped credential broker. Add network deny-by-default only if required, then test actual egress.
Derive touched paths and journal events from the enforcing broker/monitor rather than skill-reported artifacts; distinguish attempted, denied, completed and later detected effects.
